web2-scaling-with-explicit-trust-managem.text: Applications buy data and computation while terminals choose anchors and verify answers. This separates correctness trust from capacity and enables competition on availability. An own anchor preserves independence; chosen institutional publications reduce local infrastructure under explicit trust. Follow the canonical trust and availability page.

find-your-path.text: Assess trust choices and availability, or start building a terminal by reading the lightweight Web2 application definition. Follow proof composition and chainpoint sessions for the verification flow. Explore the existing projects, evidence and roadmap for delivery status.

why-terminals-should-consume-anchored-da.text: Anchored data is data whose required claim has been verified against an independently accepted root. Ledger providers and application services remain untrusted. A ledger proof authenticates an output datum carrying an application root. Follow proof composition for checking further links.

user-stories.text: The terminal selects a chainpoint with an accepted anchor root and an available provider view. In the diagram, ledger and application services remain untrusted. Roots and evidence meet at terminal verification, which enables transactions or off-chain data use. Proof construction can be delegated while verification stays in the lightweight application.

current-state.text: The project remains at design stage. The decision record owns claims and evidence limits, and the roadmap defines deliverables and acceptance criteria.
